lens: Zoomed-out fit — does this belong in the system as architected?
answer: The v4+v5 changeset solves real, named gaps (v4: multi-account multi-provider supervisor; v5: per-account × per-provider settings consistency across N accounts × 3 CLIs) with the correct architectural shape — canonical kernel + adapter, port-in-kernel, composition into AccountSnapshotProvider with zero existing-kernel surface change, route-policy/usage-window/provider-pool kernels cleanly outside, capability-registry semantically distinct (capability rows = what an agent CAN do; SettingsTemplate = what an agent IS configured with). Industry process-supervisor primitives (systemd, supervisord, K8s Deployment, Temporal, Airflow) are correctly NOT a fit — they are process-lifecycle primitives at the wrong zoom level for a per-account routing-aware fresh-subprocess pattern (v4 §A.3 Option D wins on this exact axis). However, the changeset ships FOUR concrete fit gaps relative to doctrine that was locked in the last 48 hours: (1) v4 §B.1 introduces a crate named `oya-foundry-supervisor-conformance` whose last token `conformance` is NOT in the ADR-0056 v4.1 closed 12-layer enum (kernel|domain|application|app|adapter|infrastructure|cli|rest|grpc|graphql|worker|sdk) AND not eligible for the `oya-check-*` exemption it actually qualifies for (it IS a cross-cutting check rule); (2) v5 §B.1 introduces `oya-intelligence-settings-template-adapter-fs` whose last token `fs` is also NOT in the 12-layer enum and is the canonical BC-token-misplaced-as-layer-suffix anti-shape; (3) v5 ships 3 capability-bearing artifacts (`templates/foundry-supervisor/{claude,codex,gemini}.toml`) + 1 CI lane + 1 verifier WITHOUT registering in `/registry/artifact-capabilities-registry.json`, the control plane ADR-0069 made mandatory 2026-05-13; the 9-capability declaration is absent; (4) reusable building blocks SettingsTemplate + SettingsRenderer + HookEvent + McpServerRef are not registered in `/registry/reusable-building-blocks-registry.json` and zero knowledge-graph edges are written for v5 relationships. Two BNF violations in one changeset family is not a one-off, it is a pattern: the v4 plan was approved by Architect + Critic without either reviewer catching `-conformance`. The right move is to fold the BNF correction into v5's pre-scaffold conditions (rename both crates) and to register all artifacts in the ADR-0069 control plane before merge. Architecturally everything else fits.

industry_primitives_surveyed: systemd — Linux init/service supervisor; manages process lifecycle via unit files + cgroups + socket activation; WRONG ZOOM LEVEL for v4 (v4 needs per-message fresh-subprocess spawn with routing-aware account selection; systemd's restart-policy + cgroup-scoping is generic and would require an external policy daemon to make routing decisions — that daemon becomes Option A in disguise, the rejected SPoF shape); correctly NOT adopted
supervisord (Python process supervisor) — same shape as systemd at userspace; same wrong-zoom-level reason; correctly NOT adopted; v4 §A.3 Option A rejection covers the equivalent pattern

Kubernetes Deployment / DaemonSet — pod lifecycle + restart policy + replica management; WRONG ZOOM LEVEL (v4 messages are minutes-of-work, not pod-lifetime workloads; per-account fresh-subprocess pattern is sub-second spawn cycle; K8s pod overhead would dominate; also requires cluster infra v4 does not assume); correctly NOT adopted

Temporal — durable workflow orchestration with activity retries + history persistence; WRONG ZOOM LEVEL (v4 is single-machine local supervisor; Temporal needs a cluster + DB; v4 §A.1 explicitly chose Branch Y best-effort durability over Temporal-class durable execution); correctly NOT adopted; could fit a future Workflow Studio orchestration layer, NOT supervisor

fit_rationale: ARCHITECTURAL SHAPE IS RIGHT. v4 chooses the host-injected-policy-ports + per-CLI driver pattern (§A.3 Option D) correctly over single-daemon SPoF (Option A), per-CLI binary fragmentation with broker (Option B; correctly rejected on cost-benefit at <10 msg/s sustained), and dashboard in-process coupling (Option C; rejected on 12-layer enum violation). v5 mirrors this by choosing per-provider renderer impls (§A.1.3 Option A) over discriminated-dispatch single renderer (Option B; same anti-pattern v4 rejected for SessionDriver). Industry process-supervisor primitives (systemd/supervisord/K8s/Temporal/Airflow) are correctly OUT-OF-ZOOM: v4 needs routing-aware per-message subprocess with sub-second spawn cycle, which none of those primitives provide without an external policy daemon that re-introduces the rejected SPoF shape. Industry config-drift primitives (Ansible/Kustomize/Terraform/Helm) are correctly NOT-ADOPTED-AS-DEPS under Branch Y zero-net-new-deps but the pattern provenance is REAL and SHOULD be cited in the ADR (1 sentence, not architectural debt). Existing repo primitives — architecture-map, route-policy, usage-window, provider-pool, capability-registry, openbao SecretStorePort, jsonl-supervisor-adapter, AccountSnapshotProvider — are correctly composed, semantically distinct, or extended (not duplicated). HOWEVER fit_judgment is CONDITIONAL on four corrections before scaffold time: (1) RENAME v4 crate `oya-foundry-supervisor-conformance` → `oya-check-foundry-supervisor-conformance` per ADR-0056 §line-102-104 check-namespace exemption — the crate's purpose (emitting + verifying capability registry seed conformance) IS a cross-cutting check rule and the eligible exemption exists; latent in v4 but BLOCKING v5 merge if not corrected here since v5 lives in the same plan family; (2) RENAME v5 crate `oya-intelligence-settings-template-adapter-fs` → `oya-intelligence-settings-template-adapter` per v4 sibling `oya-intelligence-jsonl-supervisor-adapter` precedent (BC-tokens=[settings,template] + layer=adapter); (3) ADD Wave 4d grit unit registering 3 templates + 2 crates + 1 lane in `/registry/artifact-capabilities-registry.json` with full 9-capability declarations per ADR-0069 (Enforcement / Verification / Validation / Autogen[idempotency_class=content-addressed-blake3] / Self-healing[VerifyMode::AutoReconcile] / Self-updating / Self-maintaining / Knowledge-graph / Claim-matrix); (4) ADD grit unit writing 4 edges to `/registry/knowledge-graph-dynamic.json` + 4 rows to `/registry/reusable-building-blocks-registry.json`. Absent these four corrections, the v4+v5 changeset drifts toward parallel-and-temporary on TWO doctrines (ADR-0056 BNF and ADR-0069 active-artifact-contract), both of which were Accepted 2026-05-13 — 1-2 days before this changeset.
findings: BNF v4.1 VIOLATION #1 (LATENT IN v4) — `oya-foundry-supervisor-conformance` last-token `conformance` is NOT in ADR-0056 v4.1 closed 12-layer enum (kernel | domain | application | app | adapter | infrastructure | cli | rest | grpc | graphql | worker | sdk). Workspace contains ZERO existing `*-conformance` crates (`ls crates/ | grep conformance` empty). v4 §B.1 introduces it as a NEW layer token without ADR justification — the canonical new-protocol-when-existing-protocol-fits anti-pattern. The crate IS eligible for the ADR-0056 §line-102 check-namespace exemption: `oya-check-<rule-name>` flat namespace, fully exempt from BNF, designated for cross-cutting check rules. The crate's verbatim purpose (`emits the capability registry seed row for each driver at its measured T-level via build.rs` and `cargo test reads emitted seed and asserts the tier-tier-tier triple equals the measured runtime behavior`) IS a cross-cutting conformance check rule. CORRECT RENAME: `oya-check-foundry-supervisor-conformance`. SEVERITY: HIGH. The v4 plan was approved by Architect + Critic per v5 header (`v4 stands unchanged: 4 crates, 49 base + 14 sub-unit grit claims, 24 acceptance rows, APPROVED by Architect + Critic`) — neither reviewer caught this. Two BNF violations in one changeset family (this one + the v5 -adapter-fs one) is a pattern, not a one-off; protecting the BNF requires renaming both before scaffold.

BNF v4.1 VIOLATION #2 (v5) — `oya-intelligence-settings-template-adapter-fs` last-token `fs` is NOT in ADR-0056 v4.1 closed 12-layer enum. v4 sibling `oya-intelligence-jsonl-supervisor-adapter` proves the canonical shape: BC-tokens=[jsonl,supervisor] + layer=adapter. The kernel guarantees there's only one fs renderer crate per provider so the `-fs` suffix carries no information; mover it INTO bc-tokens if disambiguation is needed (`oya-foundry-settings-template-fs-adapter`) OR drop entirely (`oya-intelligence-settings-template-adapter`). The check-namespace exemption is NOT eligible here (this crate is not a check rule, it does I/O renders + diffs). SEVERITY: HIGH — blocks lean-a10 / fitness-predictable-naming lane (the very binary v4 §B.1 scaffolds at tools/oya-foundry-fitness-predictable-naming/).

ADR-0069 9-CAPABILITY ARTIFACT REGISTRATION MISSING — v5 ships 3 capability-bearing artifacts (`templates/foundry-supervisor/{claude,codex,gemini}.toml`) + 1 CI lane (`lean-settings-drift`) + 1 verifier (`oya-dev-cli settings-drift`) WITHOUT rows in `/registry/artifact-capabilities-registry.json`. ADR-0069 (Accepted 2026-05-13, 2 days before this delta) mandates this registry as control plane for every active machine-readable artifact with 9 required capabilities per row. Add Wave 4d grit unit v5.19 registering with explicit per-capability status + idempotency_class=content-addressed-blake3 for Autogen (the manifest's blake3 hashing in v5 §B.2.1 already implies it). SEVERITY: HIGH — shipping an unregistered capability-bearing artifact within 48h of the foundational contract is the canonical parallel-spec-instead-of-extending-existing anti-pattern.

REUSABLE-BUILDING-BLOCKS REGISTRY OMISSION — `SettingsTemplate`, `SettingsRenderer`, `HookEvent`, `McpServerRef` are reusable primitives (Workflow Studio settings rendering in 1 year will want the same kernel; the flat-product-catalog memory directive + Workflow-is-shared memory directive expect this). Not registered in `/registry/reusable-building-blocks-registry.json` per ADR-0069 DRY-enforcement registry. Add grit unit registering with canonical_path = `crates/oya-intelligence-settings-template-kernel/src/lib.rs::SettingsTemplate` + consumers = [`oya-intelligence-supervisor-app`] + version = 1 + deprecation = null. SEVERITY: MEDIUM — prevents the duplicate-kernel that the registry exists to prevent.

KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH EDGES MISSING — ADR-0069 mandates consumes/generates/validates/enforces relationships are encoded as graph edges, not free-text path strings. v5 ships verbal claims ('renderer materializes both files'; 'composed into AccountSnapshotProvider'; 'CI lane consumes templates') without graph edges. Add grit unit writing 4 edges into `/registry/knowledge-graph-dynamic.json`: (settings-template-kernel) --generates--> (per-account on-disk settings files); (settings-template-kernel) --consumes--> (registry/accounts/*.toml); (lean-settings-drift lane) --enforces--> (settings-template artifacts); (SettingsRenderer) --reads--> (SecretStorePort). SEVERITY: MEDIUM — enables cross-cutting queries ADR-0069 §3 names as the substrate's purpose.

TEMPLATES/ DIRECTORY SEMANTIC COLLISION — Existing `templates/` root holds 12 SCAFFOLDING META-TEMPLATES (adr-template.md, design-doc-template.md, implementation-plan-template.md, runbook-template.md, etc.) consumed at doc-authoring time. v5 places RUNTIME CONFIG PAYLOADS (claude.toml, codex.toml, gemini.toml) consumed by renderer at run-time under `templates/foundry-supervisor/`. The two purposes are semantically distinct (templates-for-authoring vs canonical-base-config-payloads) and the shared root muddles them. Options: (a) move runtime payloads to `registry/settings-templates/foundry-supervisor/{claude,codex,gemini}.toml` to align with existing `registry/accounts/` + `registry/capabilities/` pattern v5 already cites; (b) keep but add `templates/INDEX.md` row explicitly documenting dual purpose + naming policy. SEVERITY: LOW — naming hygiene; affects new-contributor cognitive load + lean-a-active-artifact-contract lane query semantics.

PER-PROVIDER CRATE PRECEDENT DIVERGENCE — v4 chose `oya-foundry-account-adapter-{claude-code,codex-cli,gemini-cli}` (3 separate per-CLI crates) for SessionDriver impls. v5 chooses ONE adapter crate housing 3 renderer impls. §A.1.3 rejects Option B (one renderer with format-dispatch) for 'one impl per CLI, not one impl with discriminated dispatch' — but Option A still puts 3 impls in 1 crate. Defensible (TOML+JSON parsing is small; per-renderer crate would over-fragment) but unjustified. Either split per provider OR add explicit ADR rationale ('rendering is value-only + parse-only + small; cf SessionDriver which owns subprocess fork+exec + per-CLI hook semantics + per-CLI watchdog timing'). SEVERITY: LOW — justifiable either way; needs explicit reasoning.

ADR-0064 PACK OVERLAY SLOT ABSENT — Every µservice per ADR-0064 = canonical base + seam/adapter/pack overlay (Korea is pack #1). v5 SettingsTemplate has `provider_overrides: BTreeMap<ProviderFamilyKey, ProviderOverrides>` but NO `pack_overlays: BTreeMap<PackId, SettingsTemplateOverlay>`. A future Korea pack needing pack-specific MCP servers, hooks, or permissions would force hand-edit. Either add the slot OR explicit ADR carve-out declaring settings-template pack-agnostic by design. SEVERITY: LOW — moot today; foundational for ADR-0064 conformance + Korea-pack realization.

INDUSTRY-PRIMITIVE PRIOR-ART NOT CITED — SettingsRenderer::verify IS Ansible '--check' + '--diff' (config-drift primitive in IaC since 2012); ProviderOverrides + canonical base IS Kustomize overlay; artifact-capabilities-registry IS AWS Config + GCP Asset Inventory shape. v5 reinvents without citing. Add 1 ADR sentence acknowledging shape provenance + why hand-rolled is the right call here (Branch Y constraint + scope is 3 providers, not generic IaC + hand-rolled TOML/JSON precedent at capability-registry-app:L96). SEVERITY: LOW — provenance hygiene; protects against future reviewers reading 'novel invention' when the right read is 'inherited well-known pattern bounded by Branch Y'.

synthesis_addendum.antithesis_steelman: The v4+v5 changeset should be REJECTED as risk-of-drift on the BNF: it ships TWO crate names violating ADR-0056 v4.1's closed 12-layer enum (`-conformance` in v4, `-adapter-fs` in v5), and the v4 violation was already approved by Architect + Critic in a prior consensus round. Approving v5 without correcting both signals that the BNF is advisory, not load-bearing — and that prior approvals can grandfather violations into the BNF enum by ratification rather than amendment. Worse, v5 ships 3 capability-bearing machine-readable artifacts within 48 hours of ADR-0069 (Accepted 2026-05-13) without registering in the control plane ADR-0069 makes mandatory. Two foundational doctrines (BNF + active-artifact-contract) both Accepted 2026-05-13 are violated in a changeset Accepted-track for 2026-05-15. The right move is to BLOCK and force both corrections before scaffold begins; otherwise the workspace doctrine becomes 'whatever the most-recent plan ships' rather than 'what the most-recent ADR locks'.
synthesis_addendum.tradeoff_tension: v4's multi-account multi-provider supervisor and v5's per-account-settings-consistency lane are BOTH load-bearing for masterplan autonomous execution (memory directive 'Autonomous-implementation artifacts': 'Long-term goal: Implement the masterplan runs without user intervention'). Without v4, foundry has no daemon. Without v5, every new ProviderAccount row in registry/accounts/*.toml drifts within one onboarding cycle and v4 §B.4 step 14 silently assumes the per-provider stop-hook exists. Holding the changeset for 4 fit-gap corrections (2 renames + artifact-registry registration + knowledge-graph edges) delays autonomous execution by 1-2 grit-claim cycles. Holding for all 9 corrections (4 hard + 5 soft) delays by 3-4 cycles. The tension: ADR-0069 + ADR-0056 conformance are LOAD-BEARING (no-silent-regression memory directive: 'public contracts protected from silent change; ADR + version bump + sunset required for any breaking change'); but the gap v4+v5 closes is ALSO load-bearing. SYNTHESIS: the 4 hard corrections are file-target-independent from the existing Wave 1-5 grit units — they touch the registries + the crate names, not the implementation logic — so they parallelize at zero added wall-clock per the dispatching-parallel-agents skill. The 5 soft polish gaps land as labeled FixupTasks behind merge.
synthesis_addendum.synthesis_proposal: APPROVE v4+v5 with FOUR HARD fit gaps converted to BLOCKING pre-scaffold conditions, executable in parallel with existing Wave 1-5 grit units (zero added wall-clock): (HARD-1) Wave 1 acquires sub-task `rename-conformance-crate-check-namespace` BEFORE Cargo.toml registration — renames v4 crate to `oya-check-foundry-supervisor-conformance` citing ADR-0056 §line-102; (HARD-2) Wave 2h acquires sub-task `rename-adapter-bnf-conformant` BEFORE first grit claim on adapter crate — renames v5 crate to `oya-intelligence-settings-template-adapter`; (HARD-3) Wave 4d acquires sub-task `register-artifact-capabilities-rows` writing 5 rows to artifact-capabilities-registry.json + 1 row to lane-registry; (HARD-4) Wave 4d acquires sub-task `write-knowledge-graph-edges-and-building-blocks` writing 4 edges + 4 rows.
